German Language Levels A1 to C2 Explained: Skills, Exams, Duration & Career Benefits

Learning German is definitely among the most profitable choices to invest in your educational, career and personal development path. The most popular native language in Europe, German is highly valued by employers, universities and other multinational organizations across the world.

No matter whether you are going to study in Germany, work in a German company or just master a foreign language, you should know everything about German language levels.

According to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), German language level proficiency can be divided into six levels: A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2. Each level implies certain reading, writing, speaking and understanding skills of German.

In the following guide, we will discuss all German language levels, skills developed at each level, certification exams, duration of studying and career options.

German Language Levels Explained

Here is how CEFR divides learners according to their proficiency

Category Level Proficiency
Basic User A1, A2 Beginner to Elementary
Independent User B1, B2 Intermediate to Upper Intermediate
Proficient User C1, C2 Advanced to Near-Native Fluency

At higher levels, your communication skills will become much more natural and professional.

German A1 Level: For Beginners

The German A1 Level course is intended for absolute beginners. This course teaches the basics of the German language.

What You Will Be Able To Do at A1

  • To introduce yourself and other people
  • To ask and respond to basic questions
  • To understand common words and expressions
  • To read simple signs and instructions
  • To write simple messages and emails

Topics Covered

  • Greetings and introductions
  • Numbers and dates
  • Family and friends
  • Supermarket and food
  • Routine activities

Certification Recommended

Goethe-Zertifikat A1

TELC Deutsch A1

Duration

It takes most students 80-120 learning hours to finish this level, which equals 2-3 months of studying.

German A2 Level: Elementary

This course makes it easier for students to speak with confidence in daily life situations.

What You Are Able to Do at A2

  • Carry out routine conversations
  • Talk about your past experiences and background
  • Know common phrases
  • Writing simple letters and emails
  • Convey yourself in basic travel situations

Subjects Taught

  • Travel and transport
  • Health and lifestyles
  • Employment and education
  • Shopping and services

Suggested Test

Goethe-Zertifikat A2

TELC Deutsch A2

Duration

About 180 – 250 hours of study time is required to achieve A2 level.

German B1 Level: Intermediate

The German B1 Level: Intermediate is known as the minimum level for independent language use.

What You Can Do at B1

  • Comprehend the gist of conversation
  • Deal with most travel-related issues
  • Talk about known subjects
  • Speak about personal views and future intentions
  • Produce structured text

Subjects Taught

  • Vocational training and employment
  • Electronics
  • Culture and society
  • The environment

Suggested Exam

Goethe-Zertifikat B1

TELC Deutsch B1

Duration

To reach B1 level, students should have studied for 350 to 450 hours.

Advantages of Learning German B1 in Your Career

Vocational training and work in Germany requires German at B1 level.

German B2 Level: Upper Intermediate

The German B2 Level: Upper Intermediate is one of the most useful proficiency levels for students and professionals alike.

What You Can Do at B2

  • Communicate fluently with native speakers
  • Participate in complex conversations
  • Attend professional conferences
  • Write lengthy reports and presentations
  • Argue your point of view convincingly

Subjects Taught

  • Business communication
  • Economics
  • Politics
  • Science and technology

Examination Recommended

Goethe-Zertifikat B2

TELC Deutsch B2

Duration

It usually takes most students about 500–650 hours to reach level B2.

Career Prospects

In many instances, reaching level B2 is the minimum required for:

Corporate jobs

Business-related professions

Customer support jobs

Marketing and sales jobs

Some universities

German C1 Level: Advanced Level German

The German C1 Level: Advanced Level German shows a high level of mastery of the language in academic and professional contexts.

Skills Developed at C1

Comprehend challenging texts

Converse fluently and effortlessly

Make professional presentations

Engage in academic discussions

Compose thorough reports and research papers

Subjects Taught

  • Academic communication
  • Research and innovations
  • Professional communications
  • Advanced grammar and vocabulary

Recommended Examination

Goethe-Zertifikat C1

TELC Deutsch C1

TestDaF

Duration

It takes learners 700-900 study hours to acquire C1 level of German language.

Career Benefits

Highly demanded in

• Engineering
• Healthcare
• Finance
• Research
• Consulting
• Higher education
  • C1 level of German language is mandatory for students of many German universities that offer degrees in German.

German C2 Level: Highly Competent Level German

German C2 Level: Highly Competent Level German is the highest level of proficiency in German under CEFR.

What you can do at C2 Level?

  • Understand nearly everything you hear and read
  • Converse with high fluency
  • Use specialized vocabulary
  • Take part in complex debates
  • Be able to create complex professional and academic texts

Test recommendation

Goethe-Zertifikat C2

TELC Deutsch C2

Duration

It usually takes over 1000 hours of hard work to reach C2 level.

Professional advantages

The C2 level proficiency is advantageous for the following professionals

  • Interpreters/Translators
  • University Professors
  • Diplomats
  • Journalists
  • Legal experts
  • Senior management roles

German Language Certification Exams

Various exams to test German language ability are offered across the globe.

Exam Tested Levels Suitable For
Goethe-Zertifikat A1-C2 Global acceptance
TELC A1-C2 Educational and professional purposes
TestDaF B2-C1 Admission to universities
DSH C1 Learning in Germany
ÖSD A1-C2 German speaking nations

These certifications are accepted by companies, academic institutions, and immigration offices across the world.

Time to Study German Language

German Language Levels Time Required To Learn In Hours
A1 80-120 Hours
A2 180-250 Hours
B1 350-450 Hours
B2 500-650 Hours
C1 700-900 Hours
C2 1000+Hours

The actual duration depends on your learning pace, consistency, and exposure to the language.

Reasons for Learning German

Education Possibilities

There are some of the best universities in Germany where one can get quality education at lower costs.

Professional Success

Professionals who speak German have an edge over others in engineering, IT, medical field, finance, and international business sectors.

Global Business Advantage

Germany is one of the largest economies of the world; therefore, knowledge of German language can be helpful in international business.

Cultural Value

Speaking German can help you appreciate the culture of Germany through its movies, literature, and music.

Advantages for Immigrants and Settlers

Being fluent in German language gives an advantage while applying for study or working visas.

Conclusion

From the A1 Level: For Beginners to the German C2 Level: Highly Competent Level German you will get closer to speaking German really well. This means you can do a lot of things you want to do. You can study more get a job and even move to a new country. Learning German is very useful. It can help you in many ways.

The key to doing is to take the right classes practice every day and get ready, for big tests that people know about. If you do these things you can really learn to speak German. It is not that hard to become good at German if you take the classes and practice.

The German A1 Level: For Beginners and the German C2 Level: Highly Competent Level German are important to learn German.

FAQ

What are the A1, A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 levels in German?

The German language has a system to measure how well people can speak German. This system is called the CEFR standard of language proficiency. It has six levels:

A1 level which's for beginners

A2 level which is for people who know a little German

B1 level which is for people who know German pretty well

B2 level which is for people who know a lot of German

C1 level which is for people who are really good at German

C1 level is not the highest there is also C2 level which is for people who are almost as good as native German speakers.

Each German language level, like A1, A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 level means you can do things in German. You can listen to German speak German write in German and read German at levels of proficiency.

What Level of German is Required to Study in Germany?

The required German language level differs depending on the university and program:

Program Type Required Level
Foundation/Studienkolleg B1-B2
Bachelor's Degree (in German) C1
Master's Degree (in German) C1
English-taught programs A1-A2 (Optional)

Most German-language universities require certificates of German proficiency, such as TestDaF, DSH, Goethe-Zertifikat, TELC, at the C1 level.

What Level of German is Required to Live in Germany?

Generally, for living in Germany, A2 and B1 level will be enough.

A1-A2: Basic level of communication (conversations, shopping).

B1: Comfortable communication in almost all cases.

B2 and higher: Communication and integration becomes easy and professional.

Usually, B1 level of German proficiency is required for the application for permanent residence/citizenship.

What Level of German Is Needed to Work in Germany?

Required level of German varies depending on the profession.

Profession Recommended Level of German
Hospitality & Customer Services B1
IT and Engineering B1-B2
Business and Management B2-C1
Sales and Marketing B2
Teaching and Public Sector Positions C1

Although there may be some international companies that use English in their operations, having German at B1 or B2 will increase the chances of finding a job.

5. What Level of German Is Needed to Work in Germany as a Doctor?

To work as a doctor in Germany you need to have an understanding of the German language. You should have skills at the B2 level and also know medical terms at the C1 level, which is also called Medical German or Fachspracheprüfung.

Some things you need to work as a doctor in Germany are

  • You need to be able to speak and understand German at the B2 level
  • You need to know German at the C1 level
  • Your medical qualifications need to be recognized
  • You may need to take some professional exams to get a license

You need to be really good at speaking German so you can talk to your patients the people you work with and the hospitals and other places you work with. German is very important for doctors, in Germany.
